model_annotation: This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several model variants, comparing a Vanilla baseline against multiple configurations of StrmLLM and SepLLM. The x-axis represents the number of iterations (labeled "#Iteration"), displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss," displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot is rendered with a three-dimensional perspective. Six lines are shown: "Vanilla" in a light blue/purple color, "StrmLLM (n=64)" in orange, "SepLLM (n=64)" in green, "SepLLM (n=64)" in red (a second variant with the same n), "SepLLM (n=64, H)" in dark blue, and "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" in purple. All lines begin at high loss values near 3.3–3.4 at the start of training and decrease steeply during the early iterations before gradually flattening out. By approximately 140,000 iterations, the Vanilla line appears to settle at a higher loss value (around 2.55–2.6) compared to the other variants, which cluster together at lower loss values around 2.4–2.5. The lines exhibit noisy fluctuations throughout training, particularly visible in the Vanilla curve which shows more pronounced variance. The SepLLM and StrmLLM variants generally track closely together, with the SepLLM (n=128) and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) configurations appearing among the lowest-loss curves toward the end of training.
